q: Crops grown mainly for their edible seeds inside pods (e.g. beans, groundnuts, cowpeas) are ____. (P3)
explain: Legumes are protein-rich crops that also fix atmospheric nitrogen into the soil.

q: Crops grown for their underground swollen edible roots or stems (e.g. yam, cassava, sweet potato) are ____. (P3)
explain: Tubers store abundant carbohydrate energy underground for plant survival and human consumption.

q: Crops grown for their grain seeds (e.g. rice, maize, wheat, millet, sorghum) are classified as ____. (P3)
explain: Cereals are grass crops cultivated globally for their edible grain components.

q: Unwanted wild plants growing on farm plots that compete with crops for sunlight, water, and nutrients are ____. (P3)
explain: Weeds reduce crop yields and must be controlled by systematic weeding or organic mulching.

q: A tool with a single wheel and two handles used for transporting soil, fertilizer, and harvested crops is a ____. (P3)
explain: Wheelbarrows facilitate manual hauling of heavy bulk materials around the farmstead.

q: Crop classification: Yam is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 3).
explain: Yam is botanically classified as a tuber / root crop.

q: Crop classification: Cassava is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 3).
explain: Cassava is botanically classified as a tuber / root crop.

q: Crop classification: Rice is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 3).
explain: Rice is botanically classified as a cereal grain.

q: Crop classification: Millet is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 3).
explain: Millet is botanically classified as a cereal grain.

q: Crop classification: Sorghum (Guinea corn) is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 3).
explain: Sorghum (Guinea corn) is botanically classified as a cereal grain.

q: Crop classification: Cowpea (Beans) is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 3).
explain: Cowpea (Beans) is botanically classified as a legume.

q: Crop classification: Groundnut (Peanut) is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 3).
explain: Groundnut (Peanut) is botanically classified as a legume and oil crop.

q: Crop classification: Oil Palm is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 3).
explain: Oil Palm is botanically classified as a oil and cash crop.

q: Crop classification: Cotton is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 3).
options: fibre crop used for making textile clothing
explain: Cotton is botanically classified as a fibre crop used for making textile clothing.

q: Crop classification: Coffee is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 3).
explain: Coffee is botanically classified as a beverage crop.

q: Crop classification: Tea is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 3).
explain: Tea is botanically classified as a beverage crop.

q: Crop classification: Sugarcane is scientifically grouped as a ____ (Primary 3).
explain: Sugarcane is botanically classified as a sugar crop.

q: Animal husbandry: What major agricultural products do we obtain from Sheep? [P3]
explain: Sheep provide wool and mutton for human consumption and industrial use.

q: Animal husbandry: What major agricultural products do we obtain from Bees (Apiculture)? [P3]
explain: Bees (Apiculture) provide honey and beeswax for human consumption and industrial use.

q: Animal husbandry: What major agricultural products do we obtain from Silkworm? [P3]
explain: Silkworm provide silk fibre for textiles for human consumption and industrial use.

q: Animal husbandry: What major agricultural products do we obtain from Pigs (Swine)? [P3]
explain: Pigs (Swine) provide pork and bacon for human consumption and industrial use.

q: Animal husbandry: What major agricultural products do we obtain from Goats? [P3]
explain: Goats provide chevon meat, milk, and leather for human consumption and industrial use.
